chapter: Big bands, small groups and studio work
title: Broadway shows versus Apollo shows

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well that was the same with those Apollo shows, two hour long, but God, we used to come in off one nighters with Cab, did it many time there at the Apollo Theatre, get in there at six o'clock in the morning, the chorus girls wouldn't even go home and go to bed, because they had to rehearse that first show that day, and we'd go on and of course it was home for everybody go home and put their luggage up and come right back there and start rehearsing, get down in the hole, that was the little place where we used to rehearse, they used to call it the hole. And at the Apollo and rehearse, and we'd have about a hour or two rehearsing before the first show, and of course the first show we would call it a regular dress rehearsal. And we had acts to play the same as the Broadway show.
It must have been great on the brass players' chops.

Oh yeah. See, so one of them Broadway shows wasn't anything when you rehearse three weeks to do a show. Like Jimmy Crawford say, 'Cozy, just the same as throwing me in the briar patch, rabbit in the briar patch. And I can play this show backwards.' Tell me about the Ethel Merman show he did. He said I know it backwards by now in three weeks because with Jimmy Lunceford you had to know a show in a hour, and have it memorized in your head. Now of course the first show would be a regular dress rehearsal, but the second show would shape up a little bit better.
